definitions.gloss: prepared side dishes; ready-made dishes; deli food
definitions.explanation: Pre-cooked dishes sold at supermarkets, department store basements, or specialty shops, meant to be taken home and eaten. Includes items like fried chicken, salads, simmered vegetables, and other everyday dishes.

examples.japanese: お{惣菜|そうざい}を{買|か}って{帰|かえ}った。
examples.english: I bought some deli food on my way home.

examples.japanese: スーパーのお{惣菜|そうざい}コーナーは{夕方|ゆうがた}になると{混|こ}む。
examples.english: The deli section of the supermarket gets crowded in the evening.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しい{日|ひ}はお{惣菜|そうざい}に{頼|たよ}ることが{多|おお}いが、{栄養|えいよう}バランスには{気|き}をつけている。
examples.english: On busy days I often rely on prepared dishes, but I try to be mindful of nutritional balance.

notes:
WRITING: The お prefix is a polite/beautifying prefix. The base form {惣菜|そうざい} is also used, especially in compound words and on product labels.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{惣菜|そうざい}コーナー: deli section (of a store)
- お{惣菜|そうざい}を{買|か}う: to buy prepared dishes
- {手作|てづく}りのお{惣菜|そうざい}: homemade side dishes
- デパ{地下|ちか}のお{惣菜|そうざい}: department store basement deli food

CULTURE: お{惣菜|そうざい} is a major part of Japanese food culture. Supermarkets and convenience stores offer a wide variety, and department store basements (デパ{地下|ちか}) are famous for high-end prepared foods. Many stores discount お{惣菜|そうざい} in the evening before closing.
